title: runtime: treat optimization config apply as a transactional operation with checkpoints
author: Noah Patel
release_notes: Runtime now applies Optimization Config versions using a checkpointed transaction protocol (prepare/apply/commit) to reduce partial-apply states and make rollback safe under retries and worker churn.
body:
Context: As part of Safe apply + rollback for Optimization Configs (batching/caching/quant profiles), the runtime needs stronger guarantees than “best effort apply”. We’ve seen partial rollout states when workers restart mid-apply or when concurrent apply/rollback requests overlap. This PR updates the runtime apply pipeline to treat config application as a checkpointed transaction, with idempotent steps and durable progress markers.

What’s in this PR: 1) Introduce a checkpointed apply state machine in the worker: PREPARE -> APPLY -> COMMIT (plus ABORT for failures). Each phase is idempotent and can be retried safely. PREPARE fetches the target config version and validates runtime compatibility (model arch, quant profile support, cache toggles). APPLY performs the actual config materialization (batching heuristics, cache policy, quant kernel selection) into a staged slot. COMMIT swaps staged -> active atomically and emits a “config_active” metric/event with tags {tenant, model, region, config_version}. 2) Add an ApplyTransaction ID (tx_id) carried through logs/metrics. The controller can retry the same tx_id without causing repeated COMMIT or repeated cache invalidations. 3) Add durable local checkpoint storage (per worker) so that in-flight applies resume after restart instead of starting from scratch. Checkpoints are stored with (tx_id, config_version, phase, started_at, last_updated_at, error_code). 4) Make rollback safe under partial apply: if a rollback arrives while an apply is in PREPARE/APPLY, the worker ABORTs the in-flight tx and reverts to the last committed active version; if the apply is already COMMITed, rollback starts a new tx toward the previous version (no “in-place undo”). 5) Add guardrails to avoid thundering-herd cache invalidation: COMMIT can optionally perform a bounded “soft invalidate” (mark prefixes stale and lazily evict) for caching toggles, rather than immediate full flush. Defaults are conservative; can be tuned later via the Optimization Config fields. 6) Tests: unit tests for phase idempotency, restart resumption, and concurrent apply/rollback ordering; integration test harness that simulates worker restart between APPLY and COMMIT.

Why this approach: We want distributed, eventually consistent workers, but with per-worker correctness and observability. The checkpoint protocol makes the apply pipeline resilient to retries, worker restarts, and controller replays. It also creates a clear definition of “rolled out” at the runtime layer: active version is only updated on COMMIT.

Operational notes: - Metrics: runtime_config_apply_phase_total{phase, outcome}, runtime_config_active_version{tenant, model, region}, runtime_config_apply_duration_seconds{phase}. - Logging: All apply/rollback logs include tx_id + config_version + previous_version. - Failure behavior: If PREPARE fails (schema/compat), worker reports failure and keeps current active version. If APPLY fails (e.g., kernel init), worker ABORTs and keeps current active version.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Controller-side semantics for pausing rollouts on “stuck in APPLY” for >N minutes (tracked in ENG-4824). - Wiring quality gate signals for quant profiles (Applied ML gating) into controller decisions (tracked in ENG-4827).
commits: runtime/config: add ApplyTransaction + ApplyPhase state machine
runtime/config: implement durable local checkpoints and resume on restart
runtime/config: stage-and-swap commit path for batching/cache/quant settings
runtime/config: handle concurrent rollback by aborting in-flight tx
runtime/metrics: add phase + active version metrics tagged with config_version
tests: restart-between-phases integration test + ordering unit tests
docs: internal comments on transaction semantics and failure modes
conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): The staged slot approach looks good. One concern: COMMIT swaps batching heuristics + cache policy together; do we ever want to commit them independently? Also, can you confirm that APPLY does not mutate any global scheduler state visible to other in-flight requests?

Noah Patel (author): Good call. For now we treat the Optimization Config as an atomic unit since canary + rollback are version-based. APPLY only builds a staged “effective config” and initializes any needed kernel handles; scheduler state switches only happen during COMMIT at the request boundary (next dispatch tick). Added a comment + ensured we don’t update the shared scheduler config until commit() returns ok.

Sofia Ivanova (review): On the soft invalidate: can we ensure that enabling caching doesn’t cause a latency spike due to immediate allocations? Also, for disabling caching, do we risk holding onto too much memory if lazy eviction is slow?

Noah Patel (author): Implemented bounded soft invalidation only for toggles that would otherwise flush. For disable-cache, COMMIT marks caches non-writable and schedules a background eviction with a cap per second; we also add a safety “hard cap” where if cache bytes > threshold, we evict aggressively. I added metrics runtime_cache_eviction_backlog and a warning log when backlog persists > 5m.

Ethan Park (review): From control plane perspective, we need a crisp definition of success for apply. Is worker ‘applied’ once it reaches COMMIT? Please make sure failure reasons are structured so the controller can categorize (compat vs transient).

Noah Patel (author): Yes—worker only advertises the new version as active after COMMIT. I added error codes: COMPAT_VALIDATION_FAILED, FETCH_FAILED, KERNEL_INIT_FAILED, CHECKPOINT_IO_FAILED, COMMIT_SWAP_FAILED. These surface in the apply outcome metric + logs. Controller wiring comes in ENG-4824/ENG-4827.

Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Love the phase metrics. Please ensure they include tenant/model/region/config_version tags (required for the rollout health dashboard) and that we don’t cardinality explode on tx_id.
Noah Patel (author): Tags added for tenant/model/region/config_version. tx_id is log-only; metrics do not include tx_id. Also added sampling on debug logs in APPLY loop.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved after latest changes. The resume-on-restart test is a nice catch.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved; metrics/tags meet dashboard needs.
